Apple unveils new £1,999 foldable iPhone | BBC News
recentItems.description:
It’s almost 20 years since the first iPhone was released and since then more than three billion have sold worldwide, and Apple has now unveiled its first ever foldable iPhone. 
 
With a book-style format, the new iPhone, dubbed the Duo, is the largest ever size of the product. And with a US starting price of $1,999 (£1,475) going up to $3,200, it is also the most expensive. UK prices start at £1,999.
 
Apple's new chief executive John Ternus said the Duo was "inspired by the iPad" but called the folding features "fluid and completely intuitive."

Five dead and 86 feared missing after Philippines ferry fire | BBC News
recentItems.description:
At least five people are dead and 86 remain unaccounted for after a fire broke out on a ferry in the Philippines, the country's coastguard says.

Coastguard Captain Noemi Cayabyab says 43 people were rescued.

The fire engulfed the MV June Aster as it was taking 134 passengers and crew to Coron - a place popular with tourists.

AI expert warns it may kill all humans within a decade | BBC News
recentItems.description:
A leading safety researcher at the AI developer Anthropic has warned he believes there is a greater than 10% chance it "could kill all humans" within the next decade.

Evan Hubinger saidthe risk from the models which currently exist was "low" but the technology may develop and improve itself soon to the point where it posed an existential risk to humanity.

He did not spell out how he thought AI systems could in future result in humans being wiped out. But his comments are the latest in a series of increasingly stark warnings about AI, with the debate shifting from whether it truly poses a risk to how big that risk is.

Hubinger's intervention came  in response to comments from Jacob Coxon, an AI researcher who has just quit Anthropic and previously worked at OpenAI.  "Neither company is acting responsibly," he wrote.  "These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionise any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources."

Reeta Chakrabarti presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Joe Tidy.
